title: Chicken fried rice
summary: A quick weeknight fried rice with chicken thigh, scrambled egg, peas and spring onion, made with cold cooked rice so the grains stay separate.
ingredients: 600 g chicken thigh fillets, cut into 1.5 cm pieces
4 spring onions, thinly sliced, whites and greens separated
4 cups cold cooked jasmine rice (from about 1½ cups raw)
method: Toss the chicken pieces with the salt and white pepper, then prep the spring onions, garlic, ginger and rice, and mix the soy sauce, oyster sauce and sesame oil.
Cook the chicken in 1 tbsp oil in a large pan over high heat for 4 minutes, until golden and cooked through, then set aside.
Scramble the eggs in 1 tbsp oil over medium-high heat for 30 seconds until just set, and add them to the chicken.
Fry the spring onion whites, garlic and ginger in the remaining oil over high heat for 30 seconds, then stir-fry the cold rice and peas for 3 minutes until hot and the peas are tender.
Add the sauce mix and toss for 1 minute until evenly coloured, then return the chicken and egg for 1 minute until steaming, and stir through the spring onion greens.

stages.title: Prepare everything
steps: Cut the chicken thigh fillets into 1.5 cm pieces and toss with 1 tsp of the salt and the white pepper in a bowl.
Slice the spring onions, keeping the whites and greens in separate piles, then chop the garlic and grate the ginger.

Break up any clumps in the cold cooked rice with your fingers so the grains are loose, and mix the light soy sauce, oyster sauce and sesame oil in a small cup. Do not use freshly cooked rice, as it turns mushy in the pan.

stages.title: Cook the chicken and egg
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil in a large frying pan or wok over high heat until it shimmers, about 1 minute.
Add the chicken in a single layer and cook for 4 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden and no pink remains in the centre of the largest piece. Tip it onto a plate.
Return the pan to medium-high heat with 1 tbsp of the oil, pour in the beaten eggs and stir for 30 seconds until just set but still soft, then slide them onto the plate with the chicken.

stages.title: Fry the rice
steps: Heat the remaining 1 tbsp oil in the same pan over high heat, then add the spring onion whites, garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant but not browned.
Add the cold rice and the frozen peas and stir-fry for 3 minutes, pressing the rice against the pan, until the grains are hot, bouncing around and the peas are tender.

Pour the soy sauce mixture around the edge of the pan, toss for 1 minute until the rice is evenly coloured, then return the chicken and egg and toss for 1 minute until steaming hot, breaking the egg into small pieces.
Turn off the heat, stir through the spring onion greens, taste and add a little more soy sauce if needed, then serve straight away.

tips: Cook the rice the day before and spread it on a tray to cool before chilling, so the grains dry out and fry rather than steam.
Keep the pan very hot and don't crowd it; cook in two batches if your pan is smaller than 30 cm.
Swap the oyster sauce for an extra 1 tbsp light soy sauce if you want to keep it simpler.
variations: Use prawns instead of chicken and cook them for 2 minutes until pink and curled.
Make it vegetarian by using firm tofu or extra eggs, and use vegetarian mushroom stir-fry sauce in place of oyster sauce.
Add 1 tbsp chilli oil or a sliced red chilli with the garlic for more heat.
storage: Cool quickly and refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 1 day. Reheat in a hot pan or the microwave until steaming hot all the way through; don't freeze.

title: Chicken laksa
summary: A Malaysian-style curry noodle soup made with store-bought laksa paste, coconut milk, chicken, rice noodles and tofu puffs, ready in 35 minutes.
ingredients: 600 g chicken thigh fillets, thinly sliced
method: Fry the laksa paste in the oil over medium heat for 2 minutes, until fragrant and the oil separates.
Add the chicken with the salt and black pepper and cook 4–5 minutes, until no longer pink outside.
Pour in the stock and coconut milk, then add the fish sauce and brown sugar. Add the tofu puffs and simmer gently 10 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
Soak the vermicelli in boiling water for 5 minutes until soft, then drain.
Ladle the soup over the noodles in bowls. Top with the bean sprouts, coriander and chilli, and serve with the lime wedges.

stages.title: Fry the paste
steps: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat, then add the laksa paste and cook for 2 minutes, stirring, until it smells fragrant and the oil starts to separate.

Add the chicken, sprinkle with the salt and black pepper, and cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until the outside is no longer pink. Don't let the paste catch and burn on the base of the pan; add a splash of stock if it sticks.

stages.title: Simmer the soup
steps: Pour in the chicken stock and coconut milk, then stir in the fish sauce and brown sugar.

Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then add the tofu puffs and cook for 10 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through with no pink in the centre and the tofu has soaked up the broth. Keep it at a gentle simmer, as boiling hard can make the coconut milk split.

stages.title: Cook the noodles and serve
steps: While the soup simmers, place the rice vermicelli in a large heatproof bowl, cover with boiling water and leave for 5 minutes, until soft and no longer brittle, then drain well.
Divide the noodles among 4 bowls and ladle the hot soup, chicken and tofu puffs over the top.
Top with the bean sprouts and coriander, and add the sliced chilli if using. Serve straight away with the lime wedges for squeezing over.

tips: Use chicken thighs rather than breast, as they stay tender in the simmering broth.
Laksa pastes vary in heat, so start with less if yours is hot and add more at the end to taste.
Soak the noodles separately rather than in the soup so they don't turn soft and swell up in the leftovers.
variations: Swap the chicken for peeled raw prawns and add them in the last 3 minutes, until pink and curled.
For a vegetarian version, use vegetable stock, leave out the chicken and fish sauce, and use soy sauce instead, adding extra tofu and green beans.
storage: Keep the soup and noodles separately in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat the soup gently on the stove until steaming, and pour over the noodles. Not recommended for freezing, as the coconut milk can split.

title: Honey soy chicken stir-fry
summary: Tender chicken thigh, broccoli and capsicum in a sticky honey soy garlic sauce, served over steamed rice in about 25 minutes.
ingredients: 600 g chicken thigh fillets, cut into 3 cm pieces
1 head broccoli (about 350 g), cut into small florets
method: Cook the rice in water in a covered pan on low heat for 12–15 minutes, until tender, and toss the chicken in the cornflour, salt and pepper.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large pan on high. Cook the chicken 5–6 minutes, until golden and white through, then set aside.
Add 1 tbsp oil to the pan on medium-high and stir-fry the broccoli and capsicum 3–4 minutes, until bright green and just tender.
Stir in the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then add the soy sauce, honey, vinegar and water and simmer 2 minutes, until thickened.
Return the chicken, toss 1 minute until glossy, then stir through the sesame oil and spring onions and serve over rice with sesame seeds.

stages.title: Prep and cook the rice
steps: Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear, then cook it with 1 1/2 cups water in a covered saucepan over low heat for 12–15 minutes, until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender.
While the rice cooks, toss the chicken in a bowl with the cornflour, salt and black pepper until every piece is lightly coated.
Whisk the soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar and water together in a jug, and have the garlic, ginger, broccoli, capsicum and spring onions ready by the stove, because the cooking moves quickly.

stages.title: Sear the chicken
steps: Heat 2 tbsp of the vegetable oil in a large frying pan or wok over high heat for about 1 minute, until it shimmers.

Add the chicken in a single layer and cook for 5–6 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden on the outside and white all the way through with no pink in the centre. Avoid crowding the pan, or the chicken will steam instead of browning; cook in two batches if needed.
Transfer the chicken to a plate.

stages.title: Stir-fry the vegetables and finish
steps: Return the pan to medium-high heat, add the remaining 1 tbsp vegetable oil, then add the broccoli and capsicum and stir-fry for 3–4 minutes, until the broccoli is bright green and just tender with a slight bite.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant, taking care not to let the garlic burn.
Pour in the sauce and bring it to a simmer, then cook for 2 minutes, until it thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Return the chicken and any juices to the pan and toss for 1 minute, until everything is glossy and heated through. Remove from the heat and stir through the sesame oil and spring onions.
Serve over the rice, scattered with sesame seeds if using.

tips: Cut the chicken into even pieces so it cooks at the same rate and stays juicy.
Get the pan properly hot before adding the chicken so it browns rather than stews.
Use chicken breast if you prefer, but cook it a minute less to avoid drying it out.
Whisk the sauce before you start so nothing is rushed once the pan is hot.
variations: Swap the chicken for sliced beef rump or firm tofu, cooking the beef for 2–3 minutes only.
Add 1 sliced red chilli or 1 tsp chilli flakes with the garlic for more heat.
Use snow peas, carrot or baby corn in place of the capsicum.
storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat in a hot pan or microwave with a splash of water until steaming hot all the way through.

title: Chicken Kiev
summary: Crumbed chicken breast stuffed with garlic and herb butter, browned in a pan and finished in the oven, so it's crisp outside and juicy inside.
method: Mash the butter with the garlic, parsley, dill, lemon zest and 1/2 tsp salt, roll into a log and freeze for 10 minutes until firm. Heat the oven to 200°C fan-forced.
Cut a pocket in each chicken breast, season with the remaining salt and the pepper, and tuck in the butter.
Coat each breast in flour, egg and panko, repeating the egg and panko if any bare patches show.
Heat the oil in a large ovenproof pan over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken for 3 minutes per side, until deep golden.
Bake on a tray for 14 minutes, until crisp and 75°C in the middle. Rest 5 minutes and serve with lemon wedges if you like.

stages.title: Make the garlic butter
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C fan-forced and line a baking tray with baking paper.
In a bowl, mash the softened butter with the garlic, parsley, dill, lemon zest and 1/2 tsp of the salt until evenly combined and speckled with green.
Spoon the butter onto a piece of baking paper, roll it into a log about 12 cm long and twist the ends tight. Freeze for 10 minutes until firm, which stops it leaking out later.

stages.title: Stuff and crumb the chicken
steps: Lay each chicken breast on a board and use a small sharp knife to cut a deep pocket into the thick side, taking care not to cut all the way through.
Season the chicken inside and out with the remaining salt and the black pepper.
Unwrap the butter, cut it into 4 equal pieces and push one into each pocket. Press the opening closed and, if it gapes, secure it with a toothpick.

Put the flour, eggs and panko in three separate shallow dishes. Coat each chicken breast in flour and shake off the excess, dip it in egg, then press it firmly into the panko until fully covered. Double-dip in egg and panko if any bare patches show.

stages.title: Brown the kievs
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a large ovenproof frying pan over medium-high heat for about 1 minute, until a breadcrumb sizzles straight away.
Cook the chicken for 3 minutes per side, until the crumb is deep golden. Don't turn them too early or the crumb will tear, and don't crowd the pan.
Transfer the chicken to the lined baking tray, using tongs and handling it gently so the pockets stay sealed.

stages.title: Bake and rest
steps: Bake the chicken for 14 minutes, until the crumb is crisp and the thickest part reaches 75°C on a meat thermometer, or the juices run clear when you pierce it.
Rest the kievs for 5 minutes so the juices settle and the butter cools slightly. Remove any toothpicks and serve with lemon wedges if you like, cutting in carefully as the butter will be hot.

tips: Freeze the butter until properly firm, otherwise it melts and leaks out in the pan before the chicken sets.
Press the crumb on firmly and double-coat in egg and panko for a sealed, extra-crisp crust.
Use a meat thermometer: 75°C in the thickest part means the chicken is cooked through without drying out.
You can stuff and crumb the kievs up to a day ahead and keep them covered in the fridge, then brown and bake as directed.
variations: Swap the dill for chives or tarragon, or add a pinch of chilli flakes to the butter for some heat.
Fill each pocket with a slice of ham and a little grated mozzarella along with the butter for a cheesy version.
Use thinly sliced mushrooms and extra herbs in place of the chicken for a vegetarian version, shaping the filling into crumbed mushroom caps.
storage: Keeps in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat on a tray in a 180°C fan-forced oven for 15 minutes until hot through and crisp; the microwave makes the crumb soggy.

title: Korean fried chicken
summary: Double-fried chicken wings tossed in a sticky, sweet and spicy gochujang glaze, with a shatteringly crisp coating that holds up to the sauce.
ingredients: 1 kg chicken wings, split into drumettes and flats
method: Dry the wings, season with salt and pepper, then toss in the cornflour, plain flour and baking powder. Rest 10 minutes so the coating sets.
Warm the garlic, ginger, gochujang, tomato sauce, honey, soy sauce and vinegar in a saucepan over low heat for 2–3 minutes until bubbling, then stir in the sesame oil.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat to 160°C. Fry the wings in 2 batches for 10 minutes each until pale golden and cooked through.
Raise the heat to high, bring the oil to 190°C and fry all the wings for 3–4 minutes until deep golden and crisp.
Toss the hot wings in the glaze for 30 seconds until glossy, then top with sesame seeds and spring onions.

stages.title: Prepare the chicken
steps: Pat the wings very dry with paper towel, then toss them in a large bowl with the salt and black pepper.
Mix the cornflour, plain flour and baking powder in a second bowl, then add the wings and toss until every piece is evenly coated in a thin, dry layer.
Rest the coated wings on a rack or tray for 10 minutes so the coating sets, which helps it stay crisp and stops it falling off in the oil.

stages.title: Make the glaze
steps: Place a small saucepan over low heat and add the garlic, ginger, gochujang, tomato sauce, honey, soy sauce and rice wine vinegar.
Stir for 2–3 minutes until the glaze is bubbling gently and smells fragrant, then remove from the heat and stir through the sesame oil. Don't let it boil hard, as the honey can catch and turn bitter.

stages.title: Double-fry the chicken
steps: Pour the vegetable oil into a large heavy-based pot to a depth of about 5 cm and heat over medium-high heat to 160°C, or until a pinch of flour sizzles steadily when dropped in.

Fry the wings in 2 batches for 10 minutes each, until pale golden and cooked through, turning occasionally, then lift onto a rack. Don't crowd the pot, as the oil temperature will drop and the chicken will turn greasy.

Raise the heat to high and bring the oil to 190°C, then fry all the wings together for 3–4 minutes, until deep golden and very crisp. Cut one open to check there is no pink near the bone and the juices run clear.

stages.title: Toss and serve
steps: Put the hot wings in a large bowl, pour over the warm glaze and toss for about 30 seconds until every wing is glossy and evenly coated.
Pile onto a platter and scatter with the toasted sesame seeds and sliced spring onions. Serve straight away while the coating is still crunchy.

tips: Pat the wings completely dry before coating, as any surface moisture makes the crust soggy.
Use a thermometer if you can, because the oil temperature is what makes the double fry work.
Toss in the glaze just before serving, since the crust softens the longer it sits in the sauce.
Swap the wings for boneless thigh pieces cut into 4 cm chunks and fry for 6 minutes at 160°C, then 3 minutes at 190°C.
variations: Make it spicier by adding 1 tbsp of gochugaru or a pinch of chilli flakes to the glaze.
Use cauliflower florets instead of chicken for a vegetarian version, frying for 4 minutes then 2 minutes.
storage: Best eaten fresh, as the crisp coating softens once glazed. Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2 days; reheat on a tray in a 200°C oven for 10–12 minutes until hot and crisp again.

title: Chicken burrito bowls
summary: Spiced chicken breast over brown rice with black beans, corn, fresh tomato salsa, lettuce and avocado, ready in 30 minutes and high in protein.
ingredients: 2 x 250 g microwave brown rice pouches
400 g can black beans, drained and rinsed
method: Mix the tomatoes, red onion, lime juice, coriander and some of the salt for the salsa. Halve the chicken breasts into thin steaks and rub with the oil, spices, remaining salt and pepper.
Cook the chicken in a large pan over medium-high heat for 5 minutes, until golden. Flip and cook 4–5 minutes, until white through with clear juices.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes so the juices settle, then slice. Microwave the rice for 2 minutes until steaming.
Heat the beans and corn in the pan over medium heat for 3 minutes, until hot. Build bowls with rice, beans and corn, lettuce, chicken, salsa and avocado, with lime wedges if you like.

stages.title: Make the salsa and spice the chicken
steps: Stir the tomatoes, red onion, lime juice, coriander and 1/4 tsp of the salt together in a bowl, then set aside so the flavours mingle.
Slice each chicken breast in half horizontally to make 4 thinner steaks, which cook quickly and evenly.
Mix the paprika, cumin, garlic powder, oregano, the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and the pepper in a small bowl, then rub it over the chicken with the olive oil until evenly coated.

stages.title: Cook the chicken
steps: Heat a large frying pan over medium-high heat for 2 minutes, until a drop of water sizzles straight away.
Cook the chicken for 5 minutes on the first side, until deep golden and it releases easily from the pan. Don't move it around, or it won't brown.
Flip and cook another 4–5 minutes, until the centre is white with no pink and the juices run clear (75°C if you have a thermometer).
Transfer to a board and rest for 5 minutes so the juices settle, then slice across the grain.

stages.title: Warm the sides and assemble
steps: Microwave the rice pouches for about 2 minutes, until steaming hot, following the packet directions.
Meanwhile, put the same pan over medium heat and add the black beans and corn with a splash of water. Stir for 3 minutes, until the corn is thawed and everything is hot.
Divide the rice among 4 bowls and top with the beans and corn, lettuce, sliced chicken, salsa and avocado. Serve with lime wedges if you like.

tips: Slicing the breasts in half keeps them juicy because they cook through before they dry out.
Cook the rice from scratch ahead of time if you prefer; 1 cup of uncooked brown rice takes about 30 minutes, so start it first.
Make the spice mix in bulk and keep it in a jar for quick weeknight chicken.
Add the avocado last so it stays green and doesn't turn brown.
variations: Swap the chicken for 600 g lean beef strips or raw prawns, cooked for 2–3 minutes per side.
Make it vegetarian by using a second can of beans or a pan-fried sweet potato instead of the chicken.
Add 1 tsp chipotle in adobo or a pinch of chilli flakes to the spice rub for more heat.
storage: Keep the chicken, rice, beans and salsa in separate containers in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat the chicken, rice and beans in the microwave until steaming hot, and add the lettuce, salsa and avocado fresh.

title: Beef tacos
summary: Spiced beef mince piled into crunchy taco shells with lettuce, tomato, cheese and sour cream, ready in 20 minutes.
method: Cook the onion in the oil in a pan over medium heat for 3 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Turn the heat to high and cook the beef mince for 4 minutes, until no pink remains and it is browned.
Stir in the taco seasoning and tomato paste for 1 minute until fragrant. Season with salt and pepper.
Add the water and simmer on medium for 2 minutes until thick.
Warm the taco shells in a 160°C fan-forced oven for 2 minutes until crisp.
Fill with beef, lettuce, tomato, cheese and sour cream. Serve with lime wedges if you like.

stages.title: Prep the toppings
steps: Shred the lettuce, dice the tomatoes and grate the cheese, then put each in a small bowl.
Finely dice the onion and crush the garlic so they are ready to go, as the cooking moves quickly.
Spoon the sour cream into a bowl and cut the lime into wedges if using.

stages.title: Cook the beef
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant, taking care not to let it brown and turn bitter.
Turn the heat to high, add the beef mince and break it up with a wooden spoon. Cook for 4 minutes, until no pink remains and the edges are browned.
Stir in the taco seasoning and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute until the spices smell fragrant. Season with salt and black pepper.

stages.title: Simmer the filling
steps: Pour in the water and simmer over medium heat for 2 minutes, stirring, until the liquid thickens and clings to the mince. Don't let it dry out; add a splash more water if it looks dry.

stages.title: Warm the shells and serve
steps: Warm the taco shells on a tray in a 160°C fan-forced oven for 2 minutes, until crisp and hot to the touch.
Fill each shell with beef, then top with lettuce, tomato, cheese and sour cream. Serve straight away with lime wedges, if using, so the shells stay crunchy.

tips: Drain any excess fat from the pan after browning the mince if it looks greasy, so the filling isn't oily.
Use a hot pan and don't stir the mince constantly, so it browns instead of steaming.
Stand the shells upright in a loaf tin to keep them steady while you fill them.
variations: Swap the beef for chicken mince or pork mince, cooking until no pink remains.
Use soft flour tortillas warmed in a dry pan for 20 seconds each side instead of hard shells.
Add a drained can of black beans with the water for extra fibre and a more filling taco.
storage: Keep the cooked beef in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat in a pan over medium heat until steaming hot, adding a splash of water.

title: Chicken and vegetable stir-fry with brown rice
summary: A quick Chinese-style stir-fry of lean chicken breast and plenty of greens in a ginger, garlic and soy sauce, served on brown rice.
ingredients: 3 cm piece fresh ginger, finely grated
1 head broccoli (about 350 g), cut into small florets
method: Boil the brown rice over medium heat for 25 minutes, until tender with a slight chew. Meanwhile, slice the chicken and toss with 1 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tsp cornflour, salt and pepper.
Whisk the remaining soy sauce, cornflour, honey, sesame oil and water. Prep the capsicum, carrots, broccoli, snow peas, ginger and garlic.
Heat half the vegetable oil in a wok over high heat. Cook the chicken in two batches, 3 minutes each, until golden and white through.
Stir-fry the broccoli, carrots and capsicum over medium-high heat for 4 minutes. Add the snow peas, garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Return the chicken, add the sauce and toss 2 minutes, until glossy. Drain the rice, serve topped with the stir-fry, spring onions and sesame seeds.

stages.title: Start the rice and prep
steps: Bring a large pot of water to the boil over high heat, add the brown rice, then reduce to medium so it simmers steadily. Cook for 25 minutes, until tender with a slight chew; it will finish while you stir-fry.
Slice the chicken breasts across the grain into strips about 1 cm thick. Toss with 1 tbsp of the soy sauce, 2 tsp of the cornflour, a pinch of salt and a few grinds of black pepper.
In a small jug, whisk the remaining 2 tbsp soy sauce, the honey, sesame oil, water and the remaining 1 tsp cornflour until smooth, so the cornflour doesn't clump later.

Slice the capsicum and carrots, cut the broccoli into small florets, trim the snow peas, and finely grate the ginger and chop the garlic. Keep everything within reach of the stove, because the stir-fry moves fast.

stages.title: Cook the chicken
steps: Heat a large wok or frying pan over high heat for 1 minute, until a drop of water sizzles at once. Add 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil and swirl to coat.
Cook half the chicken in a single layer for 3 minutes, turning once, until golden outside and white right through. Cut the thickest piece open to check there is no pink, then move it to a plate.
Repeat with the remaining vegetable oil and chicken. Cooking in two batches keeps the pan hot so the chicken browns rather than stews.

stages.title: Stir-fry the vegetables and sauce
steps: Return the empty pan to medium-high heat. Add the broccoli, carrots and capsicum and stir-fry for 4 minutes, until the broccoli is bright green and the carrot is just tender but still crisp.
Add the snow peas, garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant. Take care not to let the garlic brown, as it turns bitter.
Return the chicken and any juices to the pan. Stir the sauce again, pour it in and toss for 2 minutes, until it thickens to a glossy coating and the chicken is hot through.

stages.title: Drain the rice and serve
steps: Drain the rice in a colander and let it steam-dry for 2 minutes so it isn't wet or gluey.
Divide the rice among four bowls, top with the stir-fry, then scatter over the spring onions and the sesame seeds, if using. Serve straight away while the vegetables are crisp.

tips: Cook the chicken in two batches so the pan stays hot and the meat browns instead of steaming.
Slice the chicken across the grain and keep the strips thin so they stay tender and cook quickly.
Swap the vegetables for whatever is in the fridge: bok choy, zucchini, green beans or mushrooms all work.
For a faster dinner, use two 250 g pouches of microwave brown rice instead of boiling your own.
variations: Use 600 g firm tofu, pressed and cubed, instead of chicken for a vegetarian version, browning it well before adding the vegetables.
Add 1 tsp chilli flakes or 1 sliced red chilli with the garlic and ginger for more heat.
Use 600 g raw peeled prawns instead of chicken, cooking them for 2 minutes until pink and curled.
storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat in the microwave for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring halfway, until steaming hot throughout.

title: Steak sandwich
summary: A classic Aussie steak sandwich of thin-cut steak, sweet caramelised onion, beetroot and salad on toasted Turkish bread, ready in 20 minutes.
ingredients: 2 large brown onions (about 400 g), thinly sliced
1 loaf Turkish bread (about 450 g), cut into 4 pieces
method: Cook the onions in 1 tbsp oil in a pan over medium heat for 5 minutes until soft, then add the brown sugar and cook 2 minutes until deep golden and sticky.
Season the dried steaks with the salt and pepper. Cook in the remaining 1 tbsp oil in a pan over high heat for 1–2 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through.
Rest the steaks for 2 minutes so the juices settle.
Butter the cut sides of the Turkish bread and toast them in a pan over medium heat for 1–2 minutes until golden.
Layer barbecue sauce, lettuce, tomato, beetroot, steak and onions on the bread, then top and serve.

stages.title: Caramelise the onions
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat, then add the sliced onions and cook, stirring often, for 5 minutes until soft and starting to colour.

Sprinkle in the brown sugar and cook for 2 more minutes, stirring, until the onions are deep golden and sticky, then tip them into a bowl and wipe out the pan. Don't walk away, as the sugar can catch and burn quickly.

stages.title: Cook the steak
steps: Pat the steaks dry with paper towel and season both sides with the salt and black pepper, because wet steak will steam instead of browning.
Heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in the same pan over high heat until it shimmers and just starts to smoke.

Cook the steaks in two batches for 1–2 minutes per side, until deeply browned and just cooked through with no pink raw patches in the centre, then move them to a plate and rest for 2 minutes so the juices settle. Don't crowd the pan or overcook, as thin steak turns tough fast.

stages.title: Toast and assemble
steps: Split the Turkish bread pieces in half horizontally and spread the cut sides with the softened butter.
Toast the bread buttered-side down in a clean frying pan over medium heat for 1–2 minutes, until golden and crisp, working in batches if needed.
Spread barbecue sauce over the bottom halves, then layer on the lettuce, tomato, beetroot, steak and caramelised onions, and press the tops on. Serve straight away while the bread is warm and crisp.

tips: Use minute steaks or slice a rump or sirloin steak thinly and bash it flat so it cooks in a couple of minutes and stays tender.
Make the caramelised onions up to 3 days ahead and reheat them in the pan or microwave.
Dry the lettuce well so the bread doesn't go soggy.
variations: Add 4 slices of cheddar on the hot steaks and a fried egg per sandwich for a loaded version.
Swap the steak for 600 g chicken thigh fillets, flattened and cooked 3–4 minutes per side until no pink remains.
Use chilli jam or tomato relish instead of barbecue sauce.
storage: Best eaten fresh, as the bread goes soggy. Keep leftover cooked steak and onions separately in the fridge for up to 2 days and reheat gently in a hot pan.

title: Homemade beef burgers
summary: Juicy beef patties with melted cheese, beetroot, pickles, lettuce and tomato on toasted buns, a classic Aussie burger that's ready in 30 minutes.
method: Mix the mince, onion, egg, breadcrumbs, Worcestershire sauce, salt and pepper, then shape into 4 patties about 2 cm thick.
Mix the tomato sauce and mayonnaise, drain the beetroot and pickles, and slice the tomato. Butter the cut sides of the buns.
Cook the patties in the oil in a pan over medium-high heat for 4 minutes per side, until browned and no pink remains.
Top with cheddar, cover for 1 minute until melted, then rest 2 minutes.
Toast the buns over medium heat for 1 minute until golden, then stack with sauce, lettuce, tomato, patties, beetroot and pickles.

stages.title: Make the patties
steps: Combine the beef mince, grated onion, egg, breadcrumbs, Worcestershire sauce, salt and black pepper in a large bowl and mix with your hands for about 1 minute, just until it holds together.
Divide the mixture into 4 equal portions and shape each into a patty about 11 cm wide and 2 cm thick, pressing a shallow dip into the centre of each so they stay flat as they cook.
Avoid overworking the mince, as it makes the patties tough and dense.

stages.title: Prepare the toppings
steps: Wash and dry the lettuce leaves, slice the tomato, and drain the beetroot slices and pickle slices on paper towel so the buns don't go soggy.
Mix the tomato sauce and mayonnaise together in a small bowl, then spread the softened butter over the cut sides of the buns.

stages.title: Cook the patties
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat for 1 minute, until the oil shimmers.
Cook the patties for 4 minutes without moving them, until a dark brown crust forms and they release easily from the pan, then flip and cook another 4 minutes.

Lay a cheddar slice on each patty, cover the pan with a lid or tray and cook 1 minute, until the cheese is melted and the patties are cooked through with no pink in the centre and juices running clear.
Move the patties to a plate and rest them for 2 minutes so the juices settle.

stages.title: Toast the buns and assemble
steps: Wipe the pan, then toast the buns buttered side down over medium heat for 1 minute, until golden.
Spread the sauce mixture on the bun bases, then layer on the lettuce, tomato, patty with cheese, beetroot and pickles, and finish with the bun tops. Serve straight away.

tips: Grating the onion keeps the patties moist and avoids chunks that make them fall apart.
Chill the shaped patties for 15 minutes if you have time, as they hold their shape better in the pan.
Don't press down on the patties while they cook or you'll squeeze out the juices.
Add a fried egg or a slice of bacon for the full Aussie burger with the lot.
variations: Use chicken or turkey mince and cook 5 minutes per side until no pink remains.
Swap the beef patties for a store-bought plant-based patty and cook to the packet directions.
Add sliced pineapple rings, grilled for 2 minutes each side, for a burger with the lot.
storage: Cooked patties keep in an airtight container in the fridge for 3 days or frozen for 2 months; reheat in a frying pan over medium heat for 3–4 minutes per side until hot through. Assemble the burgers fresh so the buns stay crisp.

title: Beef nachos
summary: Corn chips baked under chilli beef mince, kidney beans and melted cheese, then topped with guacamole and sour cream for an easy family dinner.
ingredients: 400 g can kidney beans, drained and rinsed
method: Cook the onion in the oil in a large pan over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until soft, add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the mince on high for 5–6 minutes until browned.
Stir in the taco seasoning and cumin until fragrant, then add the tomatoes, beans, salt and pepper and simmer on medium-low for 5 minutes until thick.
Layer the corn chips, beef and cheese on a lined tray and bake at 200°C fan-forced for 6–8 minutes until the cheese bubbles.
Mash the avocado with the lime juice, then dollop it over the nachos with the sour cream.
Top with the coriander and the pickled jalapeños if using, and serve straight away.

stages.title: Cook the chilli beef
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat, then cook the onion for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the beef mince and turn the heat to high.
Break the mince up with a wooden spoon and cook for 5–6 minutes until browned all over with no pink left; don't crowd it or it will stew rather than brown.
Stir in the taco seasoning and cumin for 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the crushed tomatoes, salt and black pepper.
Reduce the heat to medium-low, add the kidney beans and simmer for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce is thick and no longer watery.

stages.title: Assemble and bake
steps: While the beef simmers, preheat the oven to 200°C fan-forced and line a large baking tray with baking paper.
Spread half the corn chips over the tray, spoon over half the beef mixture and sprinkle with a third of the cheese, then repeat with the remaining chips and beef.
Top with the remaining cheese and bake for 6–8 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbling at the edges; watch the edges of the chips so they don't burn.

stages.title: Make the guacamole and serve
steps: Mash the avocado with the lime juice in a bowl until mostly smooth with a few small chunks, then season with a pinch of extra salt if needed.
Take the nachos out of the oven and dollop over the guacamole and sour cream.
Scatter with the coriander and the pickled jalapeños if using, and serve straight away while the chips are still crisp.

tips: Drain any excess fat from the mince after browning so the chips don't turn soggy.
Layer the chips, beef and cheese twice so more chips get a topping, not just the top ones.
Make the beef mixture up to 2 days ahead and reheat it before assembling.
variations: Swap the beef for chicken mince or a second can of beans and a diced capsicum for a vegetarian version.
Add a diced fresh chilli or a spoonful of chipotle paste to the beef for more heat.
storage: Best eaten fresh as the chips go soggy. Keep leftover beef mixture in the fridge for up to 3 days and reheat in a pan or microwave until steaming hot.

title: Mongolian beef
summary: Thin strips of beef stir-fried with spring onions in a sticky sweet soy and garlic sauce, served over steamed rice in 25 minutes.
ingredients: 600 g beef rump steak, thinly sliced against the grain
½ cup (125 ml) water, for the sauce
6 spring onions, cut into 4 cm lengths
2¼ cups (560 ml) cold water, for the rice
method: Slice the beef thinly, toss with cornflour, salt and pepper, and stir the soy sauce, brown sugar, water and oyster sauce together.
Cook the rice with its water: boil on high, then cover and cook on low for 12 minutes, until the water is absorbed.
Sear the beef in 2 tbsp oil in batches over high heat, 1–2 minutes each, until browned with no pink left.
On medium heat, fry the garlic and ginger in 1 tbsp oil for 30 seconds, then simmer the sauce 2–3 minutes until glossy and thick.
Return the beef, add the spring onions and toss 1 minute until coated. Serve over rice with sesame seeds if you like.

stages.title: Prep the beef and sauce
steps: Slice the beef across the grain into strips about 5 mm thick, which keeps it tender; slicing is easier if the steak is chilled for 10 minutes first.
Toss the beef in a bowl with the cornflour, salt and black pepper until every strip has a light, even coating.
In a jug, stir together the soy sauce, brown sugar, the ½ cup of water and the oyster sauce until the sugar mostly dissolves.
Cut the spring onions, chop the garlic and grate the ginger, then keep them close to the stove because the cooking moves quickly.

stages.title: Start the rice
steps: Rinse the jasmine rice in a sieve under cold water until the water runs mostly clear, then tip it into a medium saucepan with the 2¼ cups of cold water.

Bring to the boil over high heat, then cover, reduce to low and cook for 12 minutes without lifting the lid, until the water is absorbed and the rice is tender; leave it covered off the heat while you cook the beef.

stages.title: Sear the beef
steps: Heat 2 tbsp of the vegetable oil in a large frying pan or wok over high heat for about 1 minute, until it shimmers and just starts to smoke.
Add half the beef in a single layer and cook for 1–2 minutes, until deeply browned underneath, then toss for 30 seconds until no pink remains; transfer to a plate.
Repeat with the remaining beef, adding a little more oil if the pan looks dry. Do not crowd the pan, or the beef will steam and turn grey instead of browning.

stages.title: Make the sauce and finish
steps: Reduce the heat to medium and add the remaining 1 tbsp of oil, then the garlic and ginger, stirring for 30 seconds until fragrant but not browned.
Pour in the sauce and simmer for 2–3 minutes, until it turns glossy and thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Return the beef and any juices to the pan, add the spring onions and toss for 1 minute, until the sauce clings to the beef and the spring onions are just wilted and still bright green.
Fluff the rice with a fork, divide it among bowls, spoon the beef over the top and scatter with sesame seeds if using.

tips: Slice the beef across the grain and partly freeze it for 15 minutes beforehand to get thin, even strips.
Cook the beef in two batches so it browns rather than stews; a hot pan is the key to the caramelised edges.
If the sauce gets too thick, loosen it with a splash of water; if it's too thin, simmer it for another minute before adding the beef.
Flank, skirt or sirloin steak all work in place of rump.
variations: Swap the beef for chicken thigh fillets cut into thin strips, cooking for 4–5 minutes until golden and white all the way through.
Add 1 tsp chilli flakes or a sliced red chilli with the garlic for more heat.
Serve with steamed broccoli or bok choy alongside the rice for extra greens.
storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat in a frying pan over medium heat with a splash of water for 3–4 minutes, until steaming hot all the way through.

title: Beef and Guinness stew
summary: Chuck steak slow-braised with Guinness, onions, carrots and thyme until the beef is tender and the gravy is rich and glossy.
ingredients: 1.2 kg beef chuck steak, cut into 4 cm pieces
4 carrots (about 500 g), cut into 3 cm chunks
method: Toss the beef in the flour, salt and pepper, then brown it in the olive oil in batches over medium-high heat, 4–5 minutes per batch, until deep golden.
Cook the onions over medium heat for 6–8 minutes until soft, then stir in the garlic and tomato paste for 1–2 minutes until darkened.
Add the Guinness, scraping up the browned bits, and simmer 3–4 minutes until reduced by a third.
Return the beef to the pot with the stock, carrots, celery, thyme, bay leaves, Worcestershire sauce and sugar, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and braise in a 160°C fan-forced oven for 1 hour 45 minutes, until the beef is fork-tender.
Rest for 10 minutes, remove the thyme stalks and bay leaves, and top with parsley if using.

stages.title: Brown the beef
steps: Pat the beef dry with paper towel, then toss it in a bowl with the flour, salt and pepper until evenly coated.
Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a large heavy-based pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat until shimmering.

Brown a third of the beef for 4–5 minutes, turning occasionally, until deep golden on all sides, then transfer to a plate. Don't crowd the pot, or the beef will steam and turn grey instead of browning.
Add another 1 tbsp of oil and brown the second third for 4–5 minutes until deep golden, then move it to the plate.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp of olive oil and brown the rest of the beef for 4–5 minutes, until deep golden on all sides, then add it to the plate.

stages.title: Build the base
steps: Reduce the heat to medium and add the onions to the same pot. Cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring often, until soft and lightly golden.
Stir in the garlic and tomato paste and cook for 1–2 minutes, until the paste darkens and smells sweet.
Pour in the Guinness and scrape the browned bits from the base of the pot with a wooden spoon. Simmer for 3–4 minutes, until reduced by about a third.

stages.title: Braise the stew
steps: Preheat the oven to 160°C fan-forced.
Return the beef and any juices to the pot, then add the stock, carrots, celery, thyme, bay leaves, Worcestershire sauce and brown sugar. Stir and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Cover with a lid and transfer to the oven. Cook for 1 hour 45 minutes, stirring once halfway, until the beef is fork-tender and falls apart when pressed.

Remove the pot from the oven and rest it, uncovered, for 10 minutes so the gravy thickens slightly. Discard the thyme stalks and bay leaves, taste and adjust the salt, then scatter with parsley if using.

tips: Brown the beef in batches; crowding the pot makes it steam and costs you flavour.
If the gravy is thin after braising, simmer it uncovered on the stovetop over medium heat for 5–10 minutes until it coats a spoon.
The stew tastes better the next day, so make it ahead and reheat gently.
Serve with mashed potato or crusty bread to mop up the gravy.
variations: Add 300 g peeled potato chunks with the carrots for a one-pot meal.
Swap the chuck steak for lamb shoulder, cut into chunks, for an Irish-style lamb stew.
Top with a sheet of puff pastry and bake at 200°C fan-forced for 20 minutes for a stout pie.
storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days or frozen for 3 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat gently in a pot over medium-low heat until steaming hot, adding a splash of stock if it's thick.

title: Lamb cutlets with minted peas
summary: Pan-fried lamb cutlets served over crushed minted peas with lemon, a quick weeknight main that is on the table in 20 minutes.
method: Pat the cutlets dry, rub with half the oil, and season with the salt and black pepper.
Cook the cutlets in a very hot pan over high heat in the remaining oil, 2–3 minutes a side, until golden and pink in the centre.
Rest the lamb for 5 minutes so the juices settle.
Melt the butter over medium heat, cook the garlic for 30 seconds, then add the peas and water and cook covered for 3–4 minutes, until bright green.
Crush the peas, stir in the mint, lemon zest and juice, and serve under the cutlets with lemon wedges if using.

stages.title: Prepare the lamb
steps: Take the lamb cutlets out of the fridge and pat them dry with paper towel so they brown rather than steam.
Rub the cutlets with 1 tablespoon of the olive oil, then season both sides with the salt and black pepper.
Zest the lemon, then juice it, and chop the mint leaves and finely chop the garlic so everything is ready before you start cooking.

stages.title: Cook the lamb
steps: Heat a large frying pan over high heat for 2 minutes until very hot, then add the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil.
Add the cutlets in a single layer, working in two batches if the pan is crowded, and cook for 2–3 minutes without moving them, until deeply golden underneath.
Turn the cutlets and cook for another 2 minutes for medium-rare, or 3 minutes for medium, until the meat feels springy when pressed and is pink in the centre.
Transfer the lamb to a plate and rest it for 5 minutes so the juices settle; do not skip this or the juices will run out when you cut.

stages.title: Make the minted peas
steps: While the lamb rests, melt the butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat, then add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant but not browned.
Add the frozen peas and the water, cover, and cook for 3–4 minutes, until the peas are bright green and tender.
Take the pan off the heat and roughly crush the peas with a potato masher or fork, leaving some whole for texture.
Stir through the chopped mint, lemon zest and 1 tablespoon of lemon juice, then taste and add more lemon juice if you like.
Spoon the peas onto plates, top with the lamb cutlets and serve with lemon wedges if using.

tips: Dry cutlets and a really hot pan give you a proper crust; crowding the pan makes them grey and steamy.
Ask the butcher for French-trimmed cutlets if you want them neat, or leave the fat on for extra flavour and crisp it up on its edge for 1 minute.
Use the leftover pan juices: spoon a little over the peas for extra flavour.
Crush the peas just before serving, as they lose their bright colour if left to sit.
variations: Swap the lamb for 4 chicken thigh fillets, cooked for 5–6 minutes a side until no pink remains.
Add 100 g crumbled feta to the peas for a salty, creamy finish.
Add a pinch of chilli flakes to the garlic for a little heat.
storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days in separate airtight containers; reheat the lamb gently in a pan for 1–2 minutes and the peas in the microwave until hot. Not suitable for freezing as the lamb turns dry.

title: Steak with salsa verde and sweet potato
summary: Seared rump steak with roasted sweet potato wedges, green beans and a fresh herb salsa verde, a lean and filling weeknight dinner.
ingredients: 2 large sweet potatoes (about 900 g), cut into wedges
2 tbsp olive oil, for the wedges
600 g lean rump steak (2 steaks, about 3 cm thick)
1 tbsp olive oil, for the steak
1 cup flat-leaf parsley leaves, firmly packed
method: Roast the sweet potato wedges tossed in olive oil, salt and pepper at 220°C fan-forced for 25 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.
Finely chop the parsley, basil, capers and garlic, then stir in the mustard, vinegar, extra virgin olive oil and salt.
Boil the green beans in salted water over high heat for 3 minutes until bright green, then drain.
Rub the steaks with oil, salt and pepper and sear in a very hot pan over high heat for 3–4 minutes per side for medium-rare, until browned and springy.
Rest the steaks for 5 minutes so the juices settle, slice, and serve with the wedges, beans, salsa verde and lemon wedges if you like.

stages.title: Roast the sweet potato
steps: Preheat the oven to 220°C fan-forced and line a large tray with baking paper.
Toss the sweet potato wedges with 2 tbsp olive oil, 1/2 tsp salt and a pinch of black pepper, then spread them in a single layer with space between them so they roast rather than steam.
Roast for 25 minutes, turning once halfway, until the edges are golden and a knife slides in easily.

stages.title: Make the salsa verde
steps: While the wedges roast, finely chop the parsley, basil, capers and garlic together until very fine.
Scrape into a bowl and stir in the Dijon mustard, red wine vinegar, 80 ml extra virgin olive oil and a pinch of salt.
Taste and add a little more vinegar if it needs sharpness. Avoid using a food processor, which turns it to a dull paste.

stages.title: Cook the steak and beans
steps: Take the steaks out of the fridge, pat them dry with paper towel and rub with 1 tbsp olive oil, 1/2 tsp salt and plenty of black pepper.
Bring a small pot of salted water to the boil over high heat, add the green beans and cook for 3 minutes until bright green and just tender, then drain.
Heat a large frying pan over high heat for 2 minutes until very hot and just smoking, then add the steaks.
Cook for 3–4 minutes per side for medium-rare, until deeply browned and the steak feels springy when pressed; add 1 minute per side for medium.
Rest the steaks on a board for 5 minutes so the juices settle, then slice against the grain.
Serve the sliced steak with the wedges and beans, spoon over the salsa verde and add lemon wedges if you like.

tips: Pat the steak very dry so it browns instead of steaming in the pan.
Slice the steak against the grain to keep each slice tender.
Make the salsa verde up to a day ahead and keep it covered in the fridge, stirring in a splash of oil before serving.
Use a thermometer if you have one: 52–55°C in the centre is medium-rare.
variations: Swap the rump for chicken thigh fillets and cook 5–6 minutes per side until no longer pink inside.
Add 1 finely chopped red chilli to the salsa verde for more heat.
storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days, with the salsa verde stored separately. Reheat the wedges in a 200°C oven for 10 minutes and eat the steak cold or warm it gently in a pan.

title: Beef and black bean stir-fry
summary: Tender strips of rump steak, capsicum and onion tossed in a salty, savoury black bean sauce and served over steamed rice.
ingredients: 1 large red onion (about 200 g), cut into wedges
method: Cook the rice in water on low heat, covered, for 12 minutes until the water is absorbed, then rest 5 minutes.
Toss the sliced rump steak with the cornflour, 1 tbsp soy sauce, rice wine, salt and pepper. Mix the black bean sauce, remaining soy, sugar and water.
Sear the beef in 1 tbsp oil in a hot pan over high heat in two batches, 2–3 minutes each, until browned but still pink inside.
Stir-fry the onion and capsicum in the remaining oil for 3–4 minutes until charred at the edges, then add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Add the sauce and bubble 1–2 minutes until thickened, return the beef for 1 minute, then top with spring onions and serve over the rice.

stages.title: Prepare the beef, sauce and rice
steps: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear, then cook it in a saucepan with 3 cups of water, covered, on low heat for 12 minutes after it first boils, until the water is absorbed. Rest it, covered, for 5 minutes.
Toss the sliced rump steak in a bowl with the cornflour, 1 tbsp of the soy sauce, the Shaoxing rice wine, a pinch of salt and a pinch of black pepper, so every strip is lightly coated.
Stir the black bean sauce, the remaining 1 tbsp soy sauce, the sugar and the water together in a small jug, then set it aside with the garlic, ginger and spring onions.

stages.title: Sear the beef
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large frying pan or wok over high heat for 1 minute, until it shimmers and just starts to smoke.

Add half the beef in a single layer and cook for 1–2 minutes without moving it, until browned underneath, then toss for 30 seconds until just browned all over but still pink inside. Transfer to a plate and repeat with the remaining beef, adding more oil only if the pan looks dry. Do not crowd the pan or the beef will stew and turn grey.

stages.title: Stir-fry the vegetables and finish
steps: Return the pan to high heat, add the remaining 1 tbsp oil, then the onion wedges and capsicum. Stir-fry for 3–4 minutes, until the edges are lightly charred and the capsicum is tender but still crisp.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant, taking care not to let the garlic burn.

Pour in the sauce and bubble for 1–2 minutes, until it thickens slightly and coats the vegetables. Return the beef and its juices to the pan and toss for 1 minute, until the beef is hot and cooked to medium. Scatter over the spring onions and serve over the rice.

tips: Slice the beef across the grain as thinly as you can; freezing it for 15 minutes first makes this much easier.
Get the pan very hot before the beef goes in, and cook it in batches so it sears rather than steams.
Black bean sauce is salty, so taste before adding extra soy sauce.
variations: Use chicken thigh fillets instead of beef and cook for 4–5 minutes until no pink remains.
Add 1 sliced red chilli with the garlic for more heat.
Swap the beef for firm tofu, pan-fried until golden, for a vegetarian version.
storage: Keeps in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat in a hot pan or the microwave until steaming hot throughout.

title: Pork chops with apple
summary: Pan-fried pork chops with caramelised apple and a creamy mustard pan sauce, served with buttery greens, ready in 30 minutes.
ingredients: 4 pork loin chops (about 1 kg), bone in
2 Granny Smith apples (about 360 g), cut into wedges
method: Season the pork chops with the salt and pepper, then sear in hot olive oil over medium-high heat for 4–5 minutes, then 3–4 minutes on the other side, until golden and 63°C inside. Rest 5 minutes.
Melt the butter in the pan over medium heat and cook the apple and onion for 4–5 minutes, until golden and soft.
Stir in the mustard and thyme for 30 seconds, then add the chicken stock and simmer 2 minutes, scraping up the browned bits.
Stir in the cream and simmer 1 minute until it coats a spoon.
Boil the green beans and broccolini for 3–4 minutes until bright and tender, then drain.
Return the chops to the sauce for 1 minute and serve with the greens.

stages.title: Prep and sear the chops
steps: Pat the pork chops dry with paper towel and season both sides with the salt and black pepper; dry meat browns better than damp meat.
Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat for 1–2 minutes, until it shimmers.
Cook the chops for 4–5 minutes on one side, until deep golden and they release easily from the pan, then turn and cook 3–4 minutes more.
The pork is cooked when the thickest part reads 63°C or the juices run clear with only a hint of pink; transfer to a plate, cover loosely with foil and rest for 5 minutes so the juices settle.

stages.title: Caramelise the apple and make the sauce
steps: Reduce the pan to medium heat and add the butter, leaving the browned bits in the pan for flavour.
Add the apple wedges and onion and cook, stirring occasionally, for 4–5 minutes, until the apple is golden at the edges and the onion is soft.
Stir in the mustard and thyme for 30 seconds, until fragrant.

Pour in the chicken stock, scraping up the browned bits, and simmer for 2 minutes until reduced by about a third, then stir in the cream and simmer 1 minute until the sauce coats the back of a spoon. Do not boil hard or the cream may split.

stages.title: Cook the greens and serve
steps: While the sauce simmers, bring a medium saucepan of salted water to the boil over high heat.
Cook the green beans and broccolini for 3–4 minutes, until bright green and just tender when pierced with a knife, then drain well.
Return the chops and any resting juices to the pan for 1 minute to warm through in the sauce, then serve with the greens.

tips: Choose chops at least 2 cm thick so they stay juicy while the outside browns.
Use a pan big enough to fit all four chops without crowding, or sear in two batches.
Granny Smith apples hold their shape; softer apples turn to mush in the pan.
Swap the cream for extra stock and a splash of milk for a lighter sauce.
variations: Use chicken thigh fillets instead of pork, cooking until 75°C inside.
Replace the stock with dry cider for a sharper, more traditional sauce.
Add a tablespoon of sage instead of thyme for a classic British flavour.
storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat gently in a covered pan over low heat with a splash of stock or water until hot through; the chops freeze poorly once sauced.

title: Oven-baked fish and chips
summary: Crumbed basa fillets and potato chips baked until crisp, served with homemade tartare sauce and lemon for a lighter take on the classic.
ingredients: 4 large potatoes (about 1 kg), cut into 1 cm chips
Olive oil spray, for the fish
method: Heat the oven to 220°C fan-forced. Toss the potato chips with oil, paprika, salt and pepper, spread on a tray and bake 15 minutes, until the edges colour.
Dry the basa, season, then coat in flour, egg, and panko mixed with garlic powder. Spray the tops with oil on a second tray.
Turn the chips and bake with the fish for 12 minutes, until the crumb is golden and the fish flakes and is opaque throughout.
Mix the mayonnaise, gherkins, capers, parsley and lemon juice for the tartare. Serve with the lemon wedges.

stages.title: Bake the chips
steps: Preheat the oven to 220°C fan-forced and line two large baking trays with baking paper.
Dry the potato chips well with a clean tea towel, then toss them in a large bowl with the olive oil, smoked paprika, half the salt and half the black pepper.
Spread the chips in a single layer across one tray, leaving space between them, as crowded chips steam instead of crisping.
Bake the chips for 15 minutes on the top shelf, until the edges are starting to colour, then leave them in while you crumb the fish.

stages.title: Crumb the fish
steps: Pat the basa fillets dry with paper towel and season them with the remaining salt and black pepper.
Put the flour, beaten eggs, and panko mixed with the garlic powder into three separate shallow dishes.
Coat each fillet in flour and shake off the excess, dip it in the egg, then press it firmly into the panko so it is covered all over.
Place the crumbed fillets on the second lined tray and spray the tops lightly with olive oil, which helps the crumb turn golden.

stages.title: Bake the fish and make the tartare
steps: Turn the chips over, slide the fish tray onto the lower shelf, and bake both for 12 minutes, until the crumb is golden and the fish flakes easily with a fork and is opaque all the way through.
While they bake, stir the mayonnaise, gherkins, capers, parsley and lemon juice together in a small bowl to make the tartare sauce.
Rest the fish for 2 minutes, then serve with the chips, tartare sauce and lemon wedges. Avoid turning the fish, as the underside crumb can lose its crunch.

tips: Dry the potato chips thoroughly before oiling so they crisp rather than steam.
Press the panko on firmly so the crumb stays on the fish while baking.
Use a hot oven and a single layer on each tray; crowding gives soggy chips.
Swap basa for any firm white fish, such as flathead or hoki, adjusting the time for thickness.
variations: Use sweet potato chips instead of regular potato for a sweeter side.
Add 1 tsp lemon zest and a pinch of chilli flakes to the panko for extra flavour.
storage: Best eaten fresh, as the crumb and chips soften in the fridge. Leftover fish keeps 1 day refrigerated; reheat on a tray at 200°C for 8 minutes to re-crisp.

title: Goan fish curry
summary: White fish gently poached in a tangy coconut, tomato and tamarind sauce, served over rice for an easy weeknight curry.
ingredients: 600 g firm white fish fillets (basa), cut into 4 cm pieces
1 tsp salt, plus extra to taste
1 large brown onion (about 200 g), finely diced
3 cm piece fresh ginger, finely grated
1 cup fresh coriander leaves, roughly chopped
method: Season the fish with the salt. Dice the onion and tomatoes, grate the garlic and ginger, and slit the chillies.
Cook the onion in the oil in a large pan over medium heat for 5–6 minutes until soft and golden. Stir in the garlic and ginger for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the ground coriander, cumin, turmeric and chilli powder for 30 seconds, then the tomatoes for 3–4 minutes until pulpy.
Add the coconut milk, tamarind, sugar and green chillies. Simmer gently for 4–5 minutes until slightly thickened, then season with salt and pepper.
Add the fish and cook on low for 4–5 minutes until opaque and flaking. Top with coriander and serve with rice and lemon wedges.

stages.title: Prep the fish
steps: Cut the fish into 4 cm pieces and toss with the 1 tsp salt and the turmeric from the spice list, if you like, or simply season it with the salt and set aside.
Dice the onion, grate the garlic and ginger, chop the tomatoes and coriander, and slit the green chillies lengthways so everything is ready before you start cooking.

stages.title: Build the sauce
steps: Heat the oil in a large deep frying pan over medium heat, add the onion and cook for 5–6 minutes, stirring often, until soft and light golden.

Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 1 minute until fragrant, then add the ground coriander, cumin, turmeric and chilli powder and stir for 30 seconds until the spices smell toasty; don't let them scorch or the curry will taste bitter.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 3–4 minutes, stirring and pressing down, until they break down into a thick paste.

stages.title: Simmer and finish
steps: Pour in the coconut milk, then stir in the tamarind paste, sugar and green chillies, and bring to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat for 4–5 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly and looks glossy.
Taste and season with salt and black pepper, adding a little more tamarind if you want it tangier.

Slide in the fish pieces in a single layer and spoon sauce over them, then cook gently for 4–5 minutes until the fish turns opaque and flakes easily with a fork; stir very gently, as the fish breaks up if handled roughly, and keep the heat low so the coconut milk doesn't split.
Scatter over the fresh coriander and serve over steamed basmati rice with lemon wedges, if using.

tips: Use firm fish such as basa, barramundi or ling so the pieces hold together in the sauce.
Add tamarind a little at a time and taste, as brands vary a lot in sourness.
Make the sauce up to 2 days ahead and add the fish just before serving for the best texture.
Keep the sauce at a gentle simmer once the coconut milk is in, because a hard boil can make it split.
variations: Swap the fish for raw peeled prawns and cook for 3–4 minutes until pink and curled.
Make it vegetarian with cubes of firm tofu or cooked chickpeas instead of fish.
Add another green chilli or 1 tsp more chilli powder for extra heat.
storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days in an airtight container. Reheat gently in a pan over low heat until just hot; don't freeze, as the fish turns mushy.

title: Crispy skin barramundi with greens
summary: Pan-fried skin-on barramundi with shatteringly crisp skin, served on garlicky greens with lemon for a light, protein-rich dinner.
ingredients: 1 tbsp olive oil, for the greens
1 lemon, zested and cut into wedges
method: Dry the barramundi well, score the skin, and season with salt and pepper. Trim the broccolini and beans, and zest the lemon.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook the fillets skin-side down, pressing flat, for 5–6 minutes until the skin is golden and crisp.
Flip, add the butter, and cook 1–2 minutes until the flesh is opaque and flakes easily. Rest on a plate.
Heat the greens oil over medium-high. Cook the broccolini and beans with the water for 3–4 minutes until tender, then add garlic for 30 seconds.
Stir in the spinach, salt and lemon zest for 1 minute until wilted. Serve the fish on the greens with lemon wedges.

stages.title: Prep the fish and greens
steps: Pat the barramundi fillets very dry on both sides with paper towel, paying extra attention to the skin, because any moisture will stop it crisping.
Score the skin of each fillet lightly with a sharp knife, then season the skin side with the 1/2 tsp salt for the fish and the black pepper.
Halve the broccolini stems lengthways if they are thick, and zest the lemon, then cut the zested lemon into wedges.

stages.title: Cook the barramundi
steps: Heat the 1 tbsp olive oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat for about 1 minute, until the oil shimmers.
Lay the fillets in the pan skin-side down, pressing each one flat with a spatula for 20 seconds so the skin makes full contact and does not curl.
Cook for 5–6 minutes without moving them, until the skin is deep golden and crisp and the flesh has turned opaque about three-quarters of the way up the side.

Flip the fillets, add the butter, and cook for 1–2 minutes more, until the flesh is opaque all the way through and flakes easily with a fork. Move to a plate, skin-side up, and avoid covering them or the skin will go soft.

stages.title: Cook the greens
steps: Wipe out the pan, then heat the 1 tbsp olive oil for the greens over medium-high heat for 30 seconds.
Add the broccolini and green beans with the 2 tbsp water, and cook for 3–4 minutes, tossing often, until bright green and just tender when pierced with a knife.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, stirring, until fragrant but not browned, as burnt garlic turns bitter.
Stir through the baby spinach, the 1/2 tsp salt for the greens and the lemon zest for 1 minute, until the spinach has just wilted.
Divide the greens among four plates, top with the barramundi skin-side up and serve with lemon wedges if you like.

tips: Dry skin and a properly hot pan are what make the skin crisp, so never skip the paper towel step.
Don't move the fillets while the skin side cooks, or the skin will stick and tear.
Swap the broccolini for asparagus or zucchini ribbons depending on what looks good at the shops.
variations: Use skin-on salmon fillets instead, cooking the skin side for 4–5 minutes and the flesh side for 2 minutes.
Add 1 tsp chilli flakes with the garlic for a spicy kick.
storage: Best eaten fresh, as the skin loses its crunch once stored. Leftover greens keep in the fridge for 2 days; reheat gently in a pan.

title: Cajun basa with corn salsa
summary: Cajun-spiced basa fillets pan-fried until golden, served on rice with a fresh corn, tomato and avocado salsa.
ingredients: 1 tbsp olive oil, for the fish
1 x 300 g can corn kernels, drained
1 tbsp olive oil, for the salsa
method: Rinse the rice, then simmer it covered on low heat with water and a pinch of the salt for 10–12 minutes, until tender. Rest 5 minutes, then fluff.
Toss the corn kernels, tomatoes, avocado, red onion and coriander with the lime juice, salsa oil, remaining salt and pepper.
Pat the basa dry and coat it in the Cajun spice and flour mix.
Fry in the fish oil over medium-high heat for 3 minutes until golden, flip, then cook 2–3 minutes until opaque and flaking.
Serve the fish on the rice with the salsa and lime wedges if using.

stages.title: Cook the rice
steps: Rinse the rice in a sieve under cold water until the water runs mostly clear, then put it in a medium saucepan with 1 1/2 cups of water and 1/4 tsp of the salt.
Bring to the boil over high heat, then cover, reduce to low and cook for 10–12 minutes, until the water is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Take the pan off the heat and leave it covered for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork. Don't lift the lid while it cooks or the steam escapes and the rice cooks unevenly.

stages.title: Make the corn salsa
steps: While the rice cooks, combine the drained corn kernels, cherry tomatoes, avocado, red onion and coriander in a bowl.

Add the lime juice, the olive oil for the salsa, the remaining salt and the black pepper, then toss gently until everything is coated. Fold the avocado in gently so it stays in chunks rather than turning mushy.

stages.title: Cook the basa
steps: Pat the basa fillets dry with paper towel, then mix the Cajun spice mix and flour on a plate and press each fillet into it to coat both sides lightly.
Heat the olive oil for the fish in a large non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat for 1 minute, until it shimmers.
Cook the fillets for 3 minutes without moving them, until the underside is deeply golden and releases easily from the pan.
Flip carefully and cook for 2–3 minutes more, until the flesh is opaque all the way through and flakes easily with a fork. Basa is delicate, so turn it only once to stop it breaking apart.
Serve the fish on the rice with the salsa spooned over and lime wedges on the side if you like.

tips: Pat the fillets very dry so the spice crust browns instead of steaming.
Check your Cajun mix for salt; some are very salty, so taste the salsa before adding extra salt.
Dice the salsa ingredients while the rice cooks, but add the avocado last so it doesn't brown.
variations: Swap the basa for chicken tenderloins, cooking them 4–5 minutes per side until no pink remains.
Add 1 finely chopped fresh chilli to the salsa for more heat.
Serve in warmed tortillas with shredded cabbage instead of rice for fish tacos.
storage: Keep the fish, rice and salsa in separate containers in the fridge for up to 1 day. Reheat the fish and rice in the microwave until steaming hot; the salsa is best fresh as the avocado browns.

title: Barramundi with Thai herb salad
summary: Seared barramundi fillets served on a crunchy salad of herbs, cucumber and carrot with a sharp lime and chilli dressing, light and high in protein.
ingredients: 1 cup coriander leaves and soft stems
method: Whisk the lime juice, fish sauce, sugar, garlic and chilli until the sugar dissolves.
Dry the barramundi, rub with olive oil, and season with salt and pepper. Toss the cucumber, carrot, red onion, coriander, mint and Thai basil in a bowl.
Heat a pan over medium-high heat. Cook the fillets skin-side down for 5–6 minutes, until the skin is golden and crisp.
Flip and cook 2–3 minutes, until the flesh is opaque and flakes easily. Rest for 2 minutes.
Toss the salad with most of the dressing, plate it with the fish, then add the rest of the dressing and the peanuts. Serve with lime wedges if you like.

stages.title: Make the dressing
steps: In a small bowl, whisk the lime juice, fish sauce and brown sugar for about 1 minute, until the sugar dissolves and no grains remain.
Stir in the grated garlic and sliced chilli, then taste and adjust: it should be sharp, salty and a little sweet. Add more chilli only if you want extra heat.

stages.title: Prepare the salad
steps: Pat the barramundi fillets very dry with paper towel, rub them with the olive oil and season both sides with salt and black pepper.
In a large bowl, combine the cucumber, carrot, red onion, coriander, mint and Thai basil, but do not dress it yet, as the herbs wilt quickly once the dressing goes on.

stages.title: Cook the barramundi
steps: Heat a large non-stick frying pan or chargrill pan over medium-high heat for 2 minutes, until a drop of water sizzles straight away.

Lay the fillets in the pan skin-side down and press gently for 10 seconds so the skin stays flat. Cook for 5–6 minutes without moving them, until the skin is golden and crisp and the flesh is opaque about two-thirds of the way up the side.
Flip the fillets and cook for 2–3 minutes more, until the flesh turns opaque all the way through and flakes easily when pressed with a fork. Rest on a plate for 2 minutes so the juices settle.

stages.title: Toss and serve
steps: Pour about three-quarters of the dressing over the salad and toss gently for 20 seconds, until the leaves are lightly coated.
Divide the salad among four plates, top each with a barramundi fillet, then spoon over the remaining dressing and scatter with the chopped peanuts. Serve with lime wedges if you like.

tips: Dry skin is the secret to crisp skin: pat the fillets well and don't move them while the skin cooks.
Dress the salad just before serving, or the herbs and cucumber turn limp and watery.
Soak the sliced red onion in cold water for 5 minutes if you want a milder bite.
No Thai basil? Use regular basil, or just more mint and coriander.
variations: Swap the barramundi for salmon fillets or firm white fish, adjusting the cooking time to the thickness.
Make it vegetarian with pan-fried firm tofu and use soy sauce instead of fish sauce.
Add a pinch of chilli flakes or a second chilli to the dressing for more heat.
storage: Best eaten fresh, as the dressed herbs wilt. Keep leftover cooked fish and undressed salad separately in the fridge for up to 1 day, and eat the fish cold or reheat gently in a low oven for 5 minutes.

title: Garlic prawn linguine
summary: Juicy prawns and linguine tossed in a quick garlic, chilli, white wine and lemon sauce, ready in 20 minutes.
ingredients: 600 g raw king prawns, peeled and deveined
1 small bunch flat-leaf parsley, leaves chopped
method: Boil the linguine in well-salted water for 9 minutes, until al dente. Reserve 1 cup of pasta water, then drain.
Cook the seasoned prawns in hot olive oil over medium-high heat, 1–2 minutes per side, until pink and curled. Set aside.
Stir the garlic and chilli over medium heat for 30 seconds, until fragrant. Add the wine and simmer 2 minutes, until reduced by half.
Toss in the linguine, butter, lemon zest and juice, and half the parsley for 1 minute.
Return the prawns, add a splash of pasta water and toss 1 minute, until glossy. Season with salt and pepper, top with the remaining parsley and serve with lemon wedges.

stages.title: Prep and boil the water
steps: Fill a large pot with water, add a generous pinch of salt and bring to a rolling boil over high heat, about 6 minutes.
While you wait, pat the prawns dry with paper towel so they brown rather than steam, then season them with salt and black pepper.
Thinly slice the garlic, finely chop the chilli, pick and chop the parsley leaves, and zest then juice the lemon.

stages.title: Cook the pasta and prawns
steps: Add the linguine to the boiling water and cook for 9 minutes, stirring once in the first minute so it doesn't stick, until al dente with a little bite in the centre.
Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat for 1 minute, until it shimmers.
Add the prawns in a single layer and cook for 1–2 minutes per side, until they turn pink and curl into a loose C shape; a tight O means overcooked. Transfer them to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium, add the garlic and chilli and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant and just pale golden. Don't let the garlic brown or it turns bitter.
Pour in the white wine and simmer for 2 minutes, scraping up any browned bits, until reduced by about half.
Scoop out 1 cup of the pasta cooking water, then drain the linguine.

stages.title: Toss and serve
steps: Add the drained linguine to the frying pan along with the butter, lemon zest, lemon juice and half the parsley, and toss over medium heat for 1 minute.
Return the prawns and any juices to the pan, add a splash of the reserved pasta water and toss for 1 minute, until the sauce turns glossy and clings to the pasta. Add more water if it looks dry.
Taste and adjust with salt and black pepper, then serve straight away topped with the remaining parsley and lemon wedges if you like.

tips: Pat the prawns very dry before cooking so they sear instead of stewing in their own liquid.
Pull the prawns out of the pan while you make the sauce; they cook in minutes and go rubbery if left in.
The starchy pasta water is what turns the oil, wine and butter into a silky sauce, so don't skip it.
Slice the garlic rather than crushing it; it's less likely to burn and gives milder, sweeter flavour.
variations: Swap the prawns for scallops or firm white fish pieces, cooking until just opaque.
Make it vegetarian with 400 g sautéed zucchini and a handful of baby spinach instead of prawns.
Add 1/2 tsp chilli flakes with the garlic for more heat, or a handful of halved cherry tomatoes with the wine.
storage: Best eaten fresh, as the prawns turn tough when reheated. Leftovers keep in the fridge for 1 day; reheat gently in a pan over low heat with a splash of water.

title: Thai red prawn curry
summary: Prawns, capsicum and green beans simmered in a fragrant red curry and coconut sauce, served over jasmine rice in 25 minutes.
ingredients: 200 g green beans, trimmed and halved
800 g raw prawns, peeled and deveined, tails left on
method: Cook the jasmine rice with a pinch of salt following the packet directions, and prep the capsicum, beans and lime.
Fry the curry paste in the oil over medium-high heat for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the coconut milk, fish sauce and sugar, then simmer over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, until slightly thickened.
Simmer the capsicum and beans for 3 to 4 minutes, until the beans are bright green and just tender.
Add the prawns and cook 3 to 4 minutes, until pink, curled and opaque. Stir in the lime juice and season with salt and pepper.
Serve over the rice with the coriander and lime wedges, if using.

stages.title: Cook the rice and prep
steps: Rinse the jasmine rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear, then cook it following the packet directions with a pinch of salt in the water, so it is ready when the curry is done.
Slice the capsicum, trim and halve the green beans, and juice the lime, then keep the prawns, coriander and fish sauce within reach, because the curry cooks quickly.

stages.title: Build the curry sauce
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a large deep frying pan or wok over medium-high heat, then add the red curry paste and stir for 1 minute, until it smells fragrant and darkens slightly.

Pour in both cans of coconut milk, add the fish sauce and brown sugar, and stir well. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, until the sauce is slightly thickened and glossy; avoid a hard boil, which can make the coconut milk split.

stages.title: Cook the vegetables and prawns
steps: Add the capsicum and green beans to the sauce and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes, until the beans are bright green and just tender with a slight bite.

Add the prawns and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring now and then, until they turn pink and curl into a loose C shape and are opaque all the way through. Do not overcook them, as they turn tough and rubbery.
Stir in the lime juice, then taste and season with salt and black pepper, adding a little more fish sauce if it needs more savoury depth.
Serve the curry over the rice, scattered with the coriander leaves and with lime wedges on the side if you like.

tips: Use prawns that are fully thawed and patted dry so they do not water down the sauce.
